summary: CodeNib compiles lexical (BM25), dense (embedding), and structural (SCIP/LSP symbol graph) views of one commit behind a shared manifest and source-address contract. It serves them to coding agents via skills and an MCP adapter, with context policies (grep/read, eager injection, eager+compact). Seven studies measure retrieval tradeoffs, static vs live navigation fidelity, incremental maintenance correctness, token use, and end-to-end localization/repair on SWE-bench Verified. The authors report careful intervals and predeclared contrasts.

claims.claim: On 200 SWE-bench Verified tasks, delivering CodeNib candidates and retiring them after the first read (compact) resolves 79 vs 66 for on-demand exploration and 56 for Aider's repo map.
claims.evidence: §9.9, Fig. 14: 79 vs 66 (complete-pair +6.53 pts, task-paired CI [+1.01, +12.06], exact McNemar p=0.0294, worst-case p=0.0502 over unknown fills). Repository-clustered CI [-3.92, +17.42] spans zero; 92/200 tasks are Django. Haiku 4.5 only, one run per cell, $1 budget cap. The 56 for Aider is under eager delivery. The gain is via submission rate (98 vs 81), not accuracy (0.81 each), and narrows to +3.7 [-3.7, +11.2] at $2.

claims.claim: Behind LocAgent, CodeNib's views let the agent finish 78 of 90 runs vs 65 at lower cost.
claims.evidence: Table 4 / Fig. 13: completion 78 vs 65; tokens -43.48k [-82.01, -13.80]; cell time -18.62 s. Localization File Recall@5 +8.70 [-12.41, +29.50] is not significant. 30 tasks, one model (Qwen3.5-27B). Not an independent replication: the cohort was reused after fixing two interface defects of the authors' own; an earlier ten-task study showed a 17.5-pt deficit.

claims.claim: Selected context policies use 50-87% fewer tokens than grep/read across five models without losing localization.
claims.evidence: §9.7: selected policies use 49.9, 45.1, 44.8, 12.9, 35.8% of grep/read tokens; ΔAR@5 -0.009 to +0.067 with lower bounds above the -0.05 margin. Tasks are synthetic queries generated and judged by the same Claude 'opus' alias (CodeNib Synthesis); intervals reflect snapshot variation, not model sampling. Compaction is not uniformly dominant (Compact/Eager 123.3% for Haiku).

claims.claim: Execution success is not correctness: incremental symbol-level graph repair completes on every held-out change but matches a rebuild on only 13 of 24; vector reuse is exact on 27/30 at 40x.
claims.evidence: §9.5 and §10.1 F4/F5: 13/24 symbol repair, 27/30 held-out vector reuse at median 40.43x; 8 repos (Go, Python, Rust, TS/JS).

claims.claim: Static definitions match the live language server on 86% of requests with a 1.2 s ready point.
claims.evidence: F3: 403/470 definition requests matched; static graph loads in 1.23 s vs 6.35 s live. References match only 64%, and C/C++ references 23/75. The navigation audit reassigned 311 of 487 mismatches to the authors' own decoder bug.

patterns.note: Precomputed symbol graph (SCIP/LSP) served statically answers definitions faithfully and lets LocAgent finish more often with fewer tokens. References are less reliable.
Dense candidates delivered eagerly beat BM25 eager (69 vs 63) and Aider's repo map (56) on repair.
BM25 is ready in 0.19 s but trails dense by 17 pts file Recall@10. Grep/read baseline costs 2-8x the tokens for similar localization.
One-time retirement of delivered context helps repair under a fixed budget (+4.0-5.5 over eager, not significant after Holm), but compaction is not uniformly dominant across models.
Exposes views through a stdio MCP adapter and bound skills.
Under a USD 1 cap, shorter context converts into more turns and more submissions; the effect shrinks when the budget is doubled.
Cost-visible traces of view, provider, and token usage are what made the fidelity checks possible.
SWE-bench Verified/Multilingual based; benchmark exposure acknowledged as unknown.

methodology.sample: Q1-Q3: 100 snapshots across five language groups (SWE-bench Verified + Multilingual); Q3 1,000 navigation requests; Q4 8 repos x 5 commits; Q5 7,500 trajectories on synthetic queries; Q6 30 tasks x 3 repeats x 2 providers; Q7 200 Verified tasks x 5 policies (11 repos, 92 Django).
methodology.baselines: Grep/read on-demand, BM25 eager, Aider repo map, LocAgent native indexes, live LSP servers, full rebuilds. Current and reasonable.
methodology.models: Agents: Claude Haiku 4.5, Qwen3.5-9B/27B, Gemma 4-12B, Gemini 2.5 Flash. Q6 uses Qwen3.5-27B only; Q7 uses Haiku 4.5 only. Embedders: SweRank, Qwen3-Embed, Jina-Code; Qwen3 rerankers.
methodology.variance: Bootstrap CIs, paired and repository-clustered intervals, exact McNemar, Holm adjustment. Q7 one run per cell plus repeats on 10 tasks (outcomes flipped on 2/10 and 4/10).
methodology.ablations: Index-family ablation, eager vs compact (fixed bytes), length-cut native control, $2 budget follow-up.
methodology.contamination_controls: Benchmark exposure unknown (acknowledged). Harness-building tasks excluded from the Q7 sample.
methodology.languages: Python, Go, Rust, TS/JS, C/C++ for retrieval/navigation. Repair is Python-only. No Java.

standards.artifacts: Describes a frozen artifact, replay, and appendices, but no public code or data URL found in the text.
standards.preregistration: Partial: Q7 population, ordering, and contrasts frozen beforehand; two analyses added post hoc (disclosed).

biases.detail: End-to-end repair (Q7) uses only Haiku 4.5 and provider substitution (Q6) only Qwen3.5-27B.
Repair and localization outcomes are on Python SWE-bench Verified only; multilingual coverage is limited to retrieval/navigation fidelity.
Q5 queries are generated and judged by the same Claude 'opus' alias, then scored on the authors' own harness.
Abstract says 'overturn three assumptions' and claims to be 'the first'; the repo-clustered interval for the headline repair gain spans zero.
No public code link found despite heavy artifact description.

coi.affiliations: UC San Diego, Stanford, UC Riverside (academic).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None owned by authors. Compares against open-source Aider and LocAgent.
coi.funding: No acknowledgments section found. Discloses Codex-assisted protocol design and analysis code.
coi.detail: Academic system paper evaluating its own system. The 'GitHub' vendor hit is page boilerplate. Unusually candid threats-to-validity section.

verdict_reason: Statistically careful, with disclosed post-hoc analyses and fidelity checks that directly inform context-serving design. The headline repair result is a single model, Python-only, Django-heavy, and loses significance under repository clustering. The localization gains are not significant, and no public artifact link was found.
applicability: Directly relevant to how the Java team serves code context across 4+ ingestion repos to mixed agent hosts. (1) Build commit-pinned lexical, symbol-graph, and dense indexes once per repo and serve them via MCP, which any host can consume; this cut tokens 20-87% here. (2) Never trust incremental index updates because the update job succeeded: verify against rebuilds per repo (symbol repair matched only 13/24). Java via SCIP/LSP is untested here, so measure jdtls static-vs-live agreement before relying on a static graph. (3) Deliver candidates up front and retire them after the first read when agents run under budget caps. Caveat: no Java data, no cross-repo queries (each view is per repo and commit), and repair evidence comes from one model.
